The flight muscles of the adult tsetsee fly, Glossina austeri, undergo a number of ultrastructural changes during growth, including an increase in the volume of mitochondria and myofibrils, and a decrease in the volume of the sarcoplasm.
the volume of the myofibrils increases rapidly during early adult life, then levels off, and that the volume of mitochondria increases steadily throughout the life of the fly.
The volume of mitochondria and myofibrils of the dorsal longitudinal muscles increases with age, while the volume of sarcoplasmic material decreases.

mitochondrial volume is directly proportional to myofibril number and that the latter increases to an asymptotic level which may be related to the number of motor units.

the growth of the adult tsete fly flight muscle is not a simple process, and that there are at least three stages of growth, which are probably related to the three stages of the life cycle of the fly.

The main takeaway from our work is that
there is a period of growth in the flight muscles of the adult tsetes fly that is not associated with any change in muscle function.
the muscle volume of the adult tsete fly is not constant, as is often assumed, but increases during the first 10 days after adult emergence, and thereafter remains constant.
